title: Chapter 48
content:
The afternoon's violent altercation brought Kang Il-hyun back to the estate well ahead of his usual hour.

Taking in the pair of contorted corpses splayed out on the stone flags by the pool, Il-hyun’s face had hardened into a frigid, unyielding grimace. His clean-up crew promptly loaded the bodies into an unmarked transport and vanished down the mountain road.

How those remnants of the Choi syndicate had discovered that Il-hyun was behind Ki-tae’s decapitation was hardly a mystery—Chairman Kang had almost certainly leaked the intelligence himself.

After a protracted, low-voiced consultation with Park Tae-soo, who had just returned from supervising the disposal, Il-hyun summoned Jakyeong up to his private quarters.

Slumping into a leather armchair, Il-hyun pulled a cigarette from his silver case and lit it. The impeccable, sharply tailored corporate heir before him bore virtually no resemblance to the panting, unhinged beast who had pinned Jakyeong beneath his hips the previous night.

"It appears I owe you my life," Il-hyun said, watching the thin gray smoke curl upward. "How should I compensate you?"

Without a beat of hesitation, Jakyeong reached into his pocket, drew out the matte-black flash drive he’d lifted from Il-hyun's Seoul penthouse, and tossed it onto the coffee table.

Il-hyun arched a single dark brow. An incredulous, amused scoff broke past his lips.

"When on earth did you manage to steal this?"

"Securing this drive was one of the core stipulations in Chairman Kang's contract."

Il-hyun rolled the cigarette between his fingers, lightly brushing his thumb over his lower lip. His dark eyes glittered with genuine curiosity.

"Go on."

"The deal was to eliminate you and deliver that drive to him."

Il-hyun let out a short, dry laugh. "So you're telling me... my life was priced at a paltry three billion won?"

"Yes."

"Fuck. That’s easily the funniest joke I’ve heard all year."

"The joke is on me," Jakyeong replied flatly. "The drive was completely blank."

"And so?"

"I want the original."

The sheer audacity of the demand—standing there with an outstretched hand, treating a piece of lethal corporate collateral like a package left in a coat check—bordered on absurd. Il-hyun had indulged the boy and praised his looks, but watching him overstep so boldly gave him pause.

Yet the unblinking, deadpan focus in Jakyeong's dark eyes was dead serious.

Il-hyun ground the cigarette into the marble ashtray, interlacing his fingers over his lap. "We're partners now, aren't we? What possible use could you have for that drive?"

"Insurance."

"Insurance?"

"Things change fast in this line of work. I need a policy of my own."

Il-hyun leaned back into the plush cushions with a languid smirk, casually draping one arm along the sofa back. "Come now. Do you honestly think I’d harm my own darling?"

Despite the theatrical pout of wounded feelings, Jakyeong offered no reaction, his lashes lowering into a cool, impassive shield.

"Are you... afraid of me?"

Jakyeong didn't deny it. "I’m not asking for a handout, Director. I'm proposing an exchange."

Reaching into his inner jacket pocket, Jakyeong produced a secondary, chrome-cased thumb drive. He slotted it into his ultra-thin field laptop, spun the display around, and tapped the trackpad to play.

Il-hyun’s brows knit into a sharp line the second the screen flickered to life.

There, rendered in crisp high-definition, was the face of Chairman Kang.

[Word has reached my ears that you and Executive Director Kang have been spending quite a bit of intimate time together lately.]

On the display, the old patriarch set his porcelain teacup down, his face splitting into a cold, predatory grin.

[Do not place your absolute trust in anyone, young man. Regardless of who they may be.]

It was the precise scene from the wiretap the night before. Il-hyun’s amused posture melted away, his expression turning arctic.

On screen, Jakyeong could be seen calmly drawing a fountain pen and a pristine note pad toward himself. His hand moved across the paper in deliberate, measured strokes before angling the pad directly toward Chairman Kang’s line of sight.

[This room is currently being monitored. I am wearing a wire.]

The patriarch’s face on screen hardened into the exact mirror of Il-hyun’s current chill. Yet decades of bloody corporate survival allowed the old man to instantly reconstruct his mask of benevolent gentility.

"An old man can't help rambling when he has a captive audience, it seems."

Jakyeong’s pen swept across the pad again:

[Kang Il-hyun is actively planning your assassination.]

The moment Chairman Kang read the ink, a flicker of pure, homicidal malice flared in his rheumy eyes.

Watching the playback, Il-hyun’s dark pupils narrowed into razor points. He flicked his eyes up to Jakyeong. To deliberately pen treasonous notes to fabricate an evidentiary paper trail... what a cunning little viper.

On screen, Jakyeong jotted down a final line:

[I will handle him personally. Trust me.]

Chairman Kang stared down at the young operative for a long, heavy heartbeat, then gave a slow, deliberate nod of approval.

Jakyeong flicked an open flame to the corner of the paper, letting it drop into the crystal ashtray to burn away into ash. The hidden camera in his wire-rimmed glasses bobbed slightly as he rose and bowed.

"I shall keep your wisdom close to heart, Chairman."

A satisfied, grandfatherly smile bloomed across Chairman Kang’s face while the handwritten note crumbled into black carbon.

The video froze.

Taking in the full scope of the footage, Il-hyun threw his head back and barked a genuine laugh.

Jakyeong smoothly ejected the drive from the port and set it on the glass table. The moment Il-hyun reached forward to claim it, Jakyeong’s hand whipped out, snatching the device and tucking it securely behind his back.

"The principle of equivalent exchange. I assume you're familiar with it?"

"You truly believe this footage is worth that much?"

"This serves as undeniable forensic proof that Chairman Kang ordered your execution... but it also proves you were plotting his," Jakyeong noted calmly. "You saw how he responded."

Il-hyun gritted his teeth, a dark, dangerous smile pulling at the corners of his mouth. "Quite the clever little fox, aren't you?"

"Are you trading, or not?"

When Il-hyun merely leaned back and stared in silent assessment, Jakyeong pushed himself up from the armchair. "If you have no use for it, I'll take my leave."

Jakyeong pocketed the drive and turned toward the door.

"Sit down," Il-hyun commanded, waving a hand.

He withdrew a fresh cigarette, lit it, and inhaled deeply. Resting his head back against the leather, he blew a stream of smoke toward the ceiling molding. Jakyeong remained standing by the coffee table, waiting in silence until the cherry burned down to the filter.

Il-hyun crushed out the butt, rose to his full height, and looked down at Jakyeong.

"Close your eyes. I'll fetch it."

Jakyeong closed his eyes without argument. The heavy, measured crunch of Il-hyun's leather soles crossed the hardwood. A hidden latch clicked open, followed by the slide of a concealed compartment.

It was in his master bedroom the entire time. Jakyeong inwardly cursed his luck—he had practically risked his life infiltrating the Seoul penthouse for a decoy.

When the room fell dead quiet, Jakyeong cracked one eyelid open.

Kang Il-hyun was crouched inches from his face, dark eyes boring into his.

"Shit!"

Jakyeong recoiled with a start, nearly toppling back into the armchair.

Il-hyun merely chuckled, dangling a sleek, matte-black drive right before his eyes—an identical twin to the dummy drive Jakyeong had stolen in Seoul.

Jakyeong snatched the hardware and plugged it straight into his laptop. "I need to verify the contents first."

Il-hyun strolled back to the sofa, crossing one long leg over the other with a tilted smirk. "I'd advise against opening it. It'll rot your eyes straight out of your skull."

Ignoring the warning, Jakyeong initiated playback.

A sprawling, muscular back and a sagging, aged lower body dominated the frame, pinning down a figure beneath the sheets. The victim was an impossibly young girl—far too young to even be called a woman, and clearly foreign.

Jakyeong’s brow pinched in deep revulsion as he scrubbed through the timestamped video. The man on top was unmistakably Chairman Kang.

Unable to stomach another second, Jakyeong slammed the laptop shut, turning a nauseated, disgusted glare toward Il-hyun.

Il-hyun flashed a bitter, knowing smirk. "Told you. You should have listened."

Jakyeong yanked the drive from the port. "Repulsive."

Il-hyun let the silence hang for a heavy moment before speaking in a low, detached drawl. "Do you know how old my late mother was when her father sold her off to pay his debts and forced her into that monster's bed?"

Jakyeong said nothing.

"Sixteen."

"..."

Il-hyun snubbed out an invisible ember in the tray, his face settling into a mask of pure, clinical boredom—as if he were discussing a completely unrelated stranger.

"Is it any wonder she went completely insane? A child who should have been wearing a school uniform, dragged off by an arrogant degenerate in his twenties to breed an unwanted bastard. If that isn't a living hell, what is?"

Jakyeong had no words to offer.

Il-hyun let out a dry, breathy scoff, snatched the chrome drive from the table, and rolled it between his knuckles. "So this belongs to me now, yes?"

Jakyeong gave a curt nod, securing the black drive in his pocket. Whether it was the original master or a flawless forensic mirror was irrelevant—he had secured his leverage.

Having wrapped up the business, Jakyeong moved toward the exit, only to find Il-hyun’s eyes tracking his every step.

"Now that we've settled our business... how about a swim?"

"No," Jakyeong answered flatly. After the poisoning attempt and the knife fight by the pool earlier that afternoon, dipping a toe in the water was the last thing on his mind.

Yet Il-hyun proved relentlessly stubborn, ultimately dragging him out to the terrace by sheer persistence.

As they walked past the kitchen, the senior housekeeper watched them with an affectionate, maternal smile—evidently delighted to see the notoriously isolated heir interacting with another human being like an ordinary man.

Upstairs, Jakyeong threw on a casual black t-shirt and loose athletic shorts, stepped out to the deck, ran through a quick set of dynamic stretches, and slipped into the deep end.

Il-hyun, however, didn't bother getting wet. He simply reclined on a sun lounger, pouring himself glass after glass of high-proof whiskey. Why drag me all the way out here just to sit on the deck and drink?

Swirling his tumbler, Il-hyun’s eyes drifted across the glassy surface of the illuminated pool.

Jakyeong had ducked under for a prolonged dive, but several minutes had passed without a single ripple breaking the surface.

Il-hyun’s hand tensed around the crystal glass. He slammed the tumbler onto the patio table and strode toward the coping, his eyes searching the depths.

A split second later, Jakyeong breached the surface with a clean, wet exhale.

Moonlight caught the glistening droplets sliding down his brow. Catching Il-hyun’s rigid posture at the edge, Jakyeong offered a teasing smirk.

"Why are you hovering over there, Director? Afraid I drowned?"

Il-hyun let out an amused scoff, shook his head, and returned to his lounger.

Jakyeong drifted through the water with effortless grace, gliding from end to end like an aquatic predator. Every time he broke the surface, the ambient LED lighting combined with the moonlight to give his wet features an ethereal, almost luminous sheen.

Il-hyun placed a fresh cigarette between his lips and sparked the tip.

Jakyeong hauled himself out of the basin, wringing the excess water from his cotton shirt. He crossed the stone patio in long, purposeful strides, reached down without a word, and plucked the lit cigarette straight from Il-hyun's mouth.

Il-hyun’s eyes widened slightly in surprise before settling back into a slow, amused gleam.

Jakyeong placed the filter between his own lips and flashed a bright, boyish grin.

Il-hyun let out a quiet laugh at the sheer nerve of it. "Decided to drop all pretense and smoke openly in front of me now, have you?"

Jakyeong glanced over his shoulder toward the dark woods. "There's no one around to watch anyway, is there?"

He took a slow, deep pull, blowing a pale plume of smoke into the cool night air.

Watching the young operative sprawl lazily across the adjoining lounger, bathed in moonlight with a cigarette between his fingers, Il-hyun quietly rose to his feet.

He picked up a plush Egyptian cotton towel and stepped behind Jakyeong's chair.

Draping the terrycloth over Jakyeong’s wet head, Il-hyun began gently working the moisture from his hair. Jakyeong waved an arm up in protest, but Il-hyun brushed the resistance aside, simultaneously plucking the cigarette back from Jakyeong's lips.

Jakyeong scowled, tilting his chin up to glare.

Il-hyun drew a heavy lungful of smoke, leaned down, and pressed his mouth directly over Jakyeong’s.

Warm, gray vapor flooded down Jakyeong’s throat as a hot, slick tongue swept inside, exploring the roof of his mouth with lingering heat before pulling away with a wet click.

Il-hyun calmly resumed towel-drying his hair, as if nothing had happened.

He said we were just going for a swim... and now we're right back here.

A sudden, uncomfortable heat prickled Jakyeong’s neck. Feeling intensely self-conscious, he fixed his gaze forward on the dark tree line.

"It will dry on its own if you leave it."

Hearing the sullen mutter, Il-hyun’s fingers drifted down, lightly kneading the shell of Jakyeong’s ear.

"You'll catch a cold. Falling ill would complicate our schedule."

"You certainly put on a convincing show of caring," Jakyeong muttered dryly. "Pity you don't show that same consideration when you're fucking me into the mattress."

"Is that a request for a gentler touch tonight? Hmm?"

The fingers on his ear slid smoothly downward, trailing over his collarbone before teasing the sensitive bud of his nipple.

Jakyeong bolted off the lounger like a startled cat.

Il-hyun let out a low, vibrating chuckle, crooking an index finger in a slow, beckoning gesture.

Jakyeong shot him a venomous look and sprinted straight to the opposite end of the pool.
